title: Learning clarinet from Larry
summary: Larry started Harry on clarinet at about eight, later sent his old thirteen-key Buffet from Chicago, and brother Jimmy helped; Harry taught himself to read a little.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: 38. I never even knew about it. Uh, I wonder if you could tell us a little bit how you happened to take up clarinet. Was that your first instrument? Yeah.
Well, my brother Larry started me off when I was a little kid.
Did you use his horn at first? Yeah. I used Larry's horn.
He'd teach me little tunes, you know. Well, he was a kid himself.
What kind of a clarinet did he have? No doubt an Albert, I guess. Albert system, yeah.
Uh-huh. At that time he had, uh, I remember well, it was a buffet.
Buffet. About how many keys do you remember? Thirteen keys. Thirteen, yeah. I've seen some of those.

Then, uh, after he, uh, went up north, he was in Chicago. Of course, I knew quite a bit about the clarinet then, but I didn't own one. How old were you when you started, about? About that time, when he first started me off, I was just a little fellow about eight years old, And he'd teach me a few little simple tunes on the clarinet. But then when he left home, I didn't have a clarinet and didn't play at all. So, uh, when he got to Chicago, man, of course I was a few years older then, I decided I wanted to practice the clarinet. Yeah. So I wrote him, he sent me the old thirteen key clarinet. He bought himself a new one. And my brother Jimmy, who was a very good musician, the one I told you that played all the strings and the cornet, well, he had never tried to play a clarinet, but he did finger it and he figured it out. So he helped me along with the clarinet. And...
Did you learn to read at that time ever?
No, not at that time, but later on I got a... Self-instruct, you know, taught myself a few little things I could get by. Well...
